title: Add Twitter to it_companies
description:
Given the set `it_companies = {'Facebook', 'Google', 'Microsoft', 'Apple', 'IBM', 'Oracle', 'Amazon'}`: Add 'Twitter' to it_companies.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `add_twitter(it_companies)`, adding 'Twitter' to the given set and returning a SORTED list of the resulting set's contents (so the result is order-independent for grading).
hints: Sets have a method for adding a single new element in place.
Modify the set you were given, then turn it into something with a predictable order before returning it.
Call the set's .add() method with 'Twitter', then return sorted(it_companies).
expected_behavior: Adds 'Twitter' to the set and returns a sorted list of all elements in the updated set.
explanation: set.add() inserts a single new element into the set in place (it does nothing if the element is already present). Returning a sorted list makes the result predictable to check, since sets themselves have no guaranteed iteration order.
